title: Demographic Approach to Species Distribution Model
text: xsdm R package integrates concepts stochastic demography species distribution modelling (SDM). Instead treating environmental conditions static snapshot, xsdm uses multi-year environmental time-series together species presence/absence records : Reconstruct species’ fundamental ecological niche via maximum-likelihood estimation. Account inter-annual climate variability estimating niche breadth position. Project species’ potential geographic range current future climate scenarios. statistical underpinning described : Berti, E., Robles Fernández, .L., Rosenbaum, B., Peterson, T.., Soberón, J., & Reuman, D.C. (2025). impacts climate variability niche concept distributions species. bioRxiv. https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.10.30.621023

text: Install latest version directly GitHub: xsdm requires R ≥ 4.1 links C++ via Rcpp/RcppParallel, working compiler (e.g. Rtools Windows, Xcode CLT macOS) needed.
code: # install.packages("remotes") remotes::install_github("xsdm-project/xsdm-devel")

title: Demographic Approach to Species Distribution Model
text: package ships built-dataset (example_1) containing objects needed run complete workflow without loading external files.
code: library(xsdm)  # The example_1 dataset is a named list bundling all example objects. names(example_1) #> [1] "par_vec"                  "bio01" #> [3] "bio12"                    "env_array" #> [5] "occ_df"                   "occ_vec" #> [7] "optim_par_list"           "optim_par_vec" #> [9] "optim_par_vec_equivalent" "par_list" #> [11] "par_vec_vsp"             "par_table"  # Fit the model from the pre-built environmental array result <- optimize_likelihood(   env_dat    = example_1$env_array,   occ        = example_1$occ_vec,   num_starts = 10L )  # Inspect the best solution result$best$loglik result$best$convergence  # Convert the best math-scale parameters to biological scale best_bio <- math_to_bio(result$best$par) str(best_bio)

what: 1 · Load and prepare environmental time series
title: Demographic Approach to Species Distribution Model
text: xsdm expects bioclimatic time-series rasters — one SpatRaster per variable layer representing one year (time step). built-data cover southern New Mexico, USA, 39 years (1980–2018) using CHELSA v2.1 bio1 (mean annual temperature) bio12 (annual precipitation).
code: library(xsdm) library(terra)  # The rasters are stored as packed SpatRasters to minimise package size. # Unpack them before use. bio1_ts  <- terra::unwrap(example_1$bio01) bio12_ts <- terra::unwrap(example_1$bio12)  # Scale to interpretable units: CHELSA bio1 is in 0.1 °C → convert to °C, # and bio12 is in kg/m² → scale to match temperature magnitude. bio1_ts  <- bio1_ts  / 100 bio12_ts <- bio12_ts / 100

title: Demographic Approach to Species Distribution Model
text: env_data_array() extracts stacks environmental values locations given presence/absence data frame, returning 3-D array (locations × time × variables).
code: # Named list of raster time series (names become the variable labels) env_data <- list(bio1 = bio1_ts, bio12 = bio12_ts)  # example_1$occ_df has columns: name, x (lon), y (lat), presence (0/1) env_dat <- env_data_array(env_data, occ = example_1$occ_df) dim(env_dat) #> [1] 1000   39    2    (locations × time-steps × variables)  occ <- example_1$occ_df$presence

title: Demographic Approach to Species Distribution Model
text: optimize_likelihood() runs multiple optimizations Latin-hypercube starting points (Sobolʼ design) returns every solution sorted decreasing log-likelihood. Internally, optimization uses ucminfcpp::ucminf_xptr() compiled objective pointer.
code: result <- optimize_likelihood(   env_dat    = env_dat,   occ        = occ,   num_starts = 20L,       # increase for a real analysis   parallel   = TRUE,       # set TRUE to use future/furrr parallelism   verbose    = TRUE )  # Solutions data frame: one row per starting point head(result$solutions[, c("start_id", "loglik", "convergence")])  # Best solution result$best$loglik

title: Demographic Approach to Species Distribution Model
text: Convert best math-scale parameter vector biologically interpretable scale plot inferred log growth–environment function:
code: best_bio <- math_to_bio(result$best$par)  # key biological parameters: # mu       – optimal environmental values # sigltil  – left-side niche widths  (Inf = no left boundary) # sigrtil  – right-side niche widths (Inf = no right boundary) # pd       – maximum probability of detection (0–1) # o_mat    – rotation matrix (correlations between environmental axes) str(best_bio)  # Visualise the niche contours (two-panel: presences vs non-detections) interpret_parameters(   best_bio,   plot_indices = c(1, 2),   env_dat      = env_dat,   occ          = occ )

what: 5 · Project the range (virtual species probability map)
title: Demographic Approach to Species Distribution Model
text: habitat_suitability() uses fitted parameter list full-grid rasters return per-cell detection probabilities:
code: # Use the full raster extent (not just occurrence points) env_data_full <- list(bio1 = bio1_ts, bio12 = bio12_ts)  # Returns a tibble with x, y, probs by default prob_tbl  <- habitat_suitability(env_data_full, best_bio) head(prob_tbl)  # Or as a SpatRaster for mapping prob_rast <- vsp(env_data_full, best_bio, return_raster = TRUE) terra::plot(prob_rast, main = "Detection probability")

title: Demographic Approach to Species Distribution Model
text: profile_likelihood() fixes target parameter grid values, re-optimises others grid point, returns profile log-likelihood together likelihood-ratio confidence threshold.
code: prof <- profile_likelihood(   profile_parameter  = "mu1",       # parameter to profile (math scale)   increment_left     = 0.2,   increment_right    = 0.2,   num_steps_left     = 20L,   num_steps_right    = 20L,   alpha              = 0.95,        # 95 % LR confidence level   optim_param_vector = result$best$par,   env_dat            = env_dat,   occ                = occ,   verbose            = FALSE )  # Profile data frame: param, value_math, loglik, convergence head(prof$profile[, c("param", "value_math", "loglik")]) prof$threshold    # LR cut-off for the 95 % CI prof$found_better # TRUE if profiling found a better point than the MLE

title: Demographic Approach to Species Distribution Model
text: xsdm model partial non-identifiability (parameters defined equivalence class), ordinary Euclidean distance appropriate. dist_between_params() uses Hungarian algorithm find equivalence-class representative p1 closest p2:
code: # Both representations belong to the same equivalence class → distance ≈ 0 dist_between_params(   p1 = example_1$optim_par_vec,   p2 = example_1$optim_par_vec_equivalent )

title: Converts parameters from the biological scale to the math (unconstrained) scale — bio_to_math
text: Transformations: - `mu`      : identity - `sigltil` : `log()` - `sigrtil` : `log()` - `ctil`    : identity - `pd`      : `logit()` - `o_mat`   : lower-triangular parameters recovered via               `extract_orthogonal_matrix_parameters()` (see Details) `o_mat` entries mapped vector via principal matrix logarithm, .e., one (skew-symmetric) matrices S `o_mat = expm(S)`. math-scale parameters `o_par` strictly lower-triangular elements `S`. `p = 1`, `o_par` entries. Note, however, principal logarithm defined special orthogonal matrices (even though matrices image matrix exponential), function may fail valid `o_mat` inputs.

title: Converts parameters from the biological scale to the math (unconstrained) scale — bio_to_math
code: ## --- p = 1 (no o_par entries) --- mu1 <- 10 sigltil1 <- 1.2 sigrtil1 <- 0.8 bio_parameters <- list(   mu      = c(mu1),   sigltil = c(sigltil1),   sigrtil = c(sigrtil1),   ctil    = 0.3,   pd      = 0.85,   o_mat   = matrix(1, 1, 1) # 1x1 orthogonal ) math1 <- bio_to_math(bio_parameters) # Canonical names names(math1) #> [1] "mu1"      "sigltil1" "sigrtil1" "ctil"     "pd"       # Back to biological scale math_parameters <- math_to_bio(math1) all.equal(math_parameters$mu, bio_parameters$mu) #> [1] TRUE all.equal(math_parameters$sigltil, bio_parameters$sigltil) #> [1] TRUE all.equal(math_parameters$sigrtil, bio_parameters$sigrtil) #> [1] TRUE all.equal(math_parameters$ctil, bio_parameters$ctil) #> [1] TRUE all.equal(math_parameters$pd, bio_parameters$pd) #> [1] TRUE  ## --- p = 2 (includes one o_par) --- mu2 <- c(11, 5) sigltil2 <- c(1.1, 1.5) sigrtil2 <- c(1.4, 1.3) ctil2 <- -0.2 pd2 <- 0.9 o_par2 <- 0.25 O2 <- build_orthogonal_matrix(o_par2) bio_parameters_2d <- list(   mu      = mu2,   sigltil = sigltil2,   sigrtil = sigrtil2,   ctil    = ctil2,   pd      = pd2,   o_mat   = O2 ) math_parameters_2d <- bio_to_math(bio_parameters_2d) # check canonical name order produced by make_mask_names(2) identical(names(math_parameters_2d), names(make_mask_names(2))) #> [1] TRUE

text: Constructs \(k \times k\) orthogonal matrix \(O\) exponentiating skew-symmetric matrix \(S\) built assigning lower-triangular entries input vector. Specifically, function sets \(S_{ij}\) (\(>j\)) `entries`, mirrors enforce \(S = L - L^\top\), returns `expm::expm(S)`, guaranteed orthogonal \(\exp(S)\) orthogonal whenever \(S\) real skew-symmetric.

title: Build an orthogonal matrix from a real-parameter vector — build_orthogonal_matrix
text: dimension `k` inferred `length(entries)` via relation \(n = k(k-1)/2\), `length(entries)` must equal triangular number. - Dimension inference uses \(k = \frac{1 + \sqrt{1 + 8n}}{2}\)   \(n = \text{length(entries)}\). \(k\) integer, input   invalid error thrown. - Orthogonality follows fact \(S^\top = -S\) implies   \(\exp(S)^\top \exp(S) = \). - Note function actually returns special orthogonal matrix, .e.,   determinant +1.
